_spec: BANZA resilience matrix — failure modes, blast radius and recovery, per component
_status: NON-NORMATIVE. This matrix records what has been examined and what was found. It points at normative authorities and at executed tests; it defines nothing. Absence of a row is not a claim of resilience — it is an unexamined component.
_boundary: Protocol resilience (what the normative architecture supports), reference-implementation resilience (what the current software demonstrates) and deployment resilience (replicas, failover, backups, geographic redundancy) are different things. This matrix covers the first two. It makes NO deployment availability claim, and no SLA, RTO or RPO is defined anywhere in BANZA.

failure_modes.F6: duplicate or replay after uncertain delivery
failure_modes.F7: trust publication unavailable, stale or invalid

fault_containment_domains.if_it_fails: verification stops locally; nothing is accepted on weaker evidence
fault_containment_domains.does_not_fail: other verifiers, other operators, already-issued evidence

fault_containment_domains.if_it_fails: material that cannot be established is refused
fault_containment_domains.does_not_fail: the historical validity of material already validly authenticated and unexpired

fault_containment_domains.if_it_fails: the target cannot be resolved; nothing is assumed about it
fault_containment_domains.does_not_fail: trust decisions over material already held

fault_containment_domains.if_it_fails: routing to the affected peer stops

fault_containment_domains.does_not_fail: anything on a verification path — BanzAI decides nothing
the cryptographic validity of artifacts already held

rows.safe_behaviour: the surviving two authorities authorise a successor set that replaces the third, without its participation
rows.forbidden_behaviour: requiring the removed authority to consent to its own removal, which would make recovery 3-of-3
rows.blast_radius: none beyond the Root plane; delegated keys and issued evidence are unaffected
rows.recovery: deterministic — a successor set at sequence N+1 authorised by the predecessor threshold

rows.safe_behaviour: canonical continuity blocks; the single survivor cannot restore the Root
rows.forbidden_behaviour: an emergency master key, a hidden recovery key, an administrator override or any single-signer break glass
rows.blast_radius: Root succession only; already-valid delegated material remains valid until it expires
rows.recovery: governance, not cryptography; may end in credible exit under a different pinned anchor, which does not inherit canonical lineage

rows.safe_behaviour: trusted state is two values (sequence, digest); restoring them reproduces every decision
rows.forbidden_behaviour: losing anti-rollback state across a restart, so a superseded set becomes acceptable again
rows.recovery: deterministic — state is rebuilt from the persisted pair

rows.safe_behaviour: two different sets at one position are a conflict; trusted state is unchanged and stays unchanged
rows.forbidden_behaviour: first arrival wins, last arrival wins, digest ordering, source preference, or any silent second write
rows.blast_radius: one verifier; the conflict is local and does not propagate
rows.recovery: governance resolves which lineage is canonical; the verifier does not guess

rows.safe_behaviour: material already validly authenticated and unexpired keeps the validity it had; a failed refresh does not rewrite history
rows.forbidden_behaviour: extending an expiry because publication is unavailable; replacing good state with malformed, unsigned, rolled-back or transport-error content; trusting the first root observed when the anchor is missing
rows.blast_radius: new material cannot be obtained; existing evaluation is unaffected
rows.recovery: refresh succeeds and the ordinary rules resume

rows.safe_behaviour: the protocol core is unaffected; verification, trust evaluation and conformance continue with no BanzAI involvement
rows.forbidden_behaviour: any verification path falling back to a language model, or BanzAI becoming required for a protocol decision
rows.recovery: none required — BanzAI is not on any critical path

rows.safe_behaviour: artifacts already held remain cryptographically valid; validity was never a property of the host
rows.forbidden_behaviour: treating a reachable origin as evidence of validity, or an unreachable one as evidence of invalidity

rows.safe_behaviour: operations that genuinely depend on the peer fail explicitly; unrelated activity continues
rows.forbidden_behaviour: marking a peer-dependent operation successful when the peer never confirmed it
rows.recovery: retry under idempotency semantics once the peer returns

rows.safe_behaviour: deterministic rejection with a reason; the process survives
rows.forbidden_behaviour: panic on untrusted input, unbounded allocation, or silent repair of malformed material

not_examined.why: clock skew: BANZA validity fields are absolute instants compared against the verifier's clock. No distributed clock is defined and none is planned. The assumption is stated rather than tested, and is recorded here so it is not mistaken for an examined property.

persistent state failure at the storage layer is a deployment concern; the protocol's requirement is only that a state advance not be reported durable when persistence failed. The reference verifier holds trusted state in the caller's hands (two values), so it has no storage layer of its own to fail.
